First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{40} & =\sqrt[3]{8\cdot 5}=\sqrt[3]{8}\cdot \sqrt[3]{5}=2\sqrt[3]{5} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt[3]{5}+5\sqrt{10}-3\sqrt[3]{40} & = \\ 2\sqrt[3]{5}+5\sqrt{10}-3(2\sqrt[3]{5}) & = \\ 2\sqrt[3]{5}+5\sqrt{10}-6\sqrt[3]{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt[3]{5}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt[3]{5}+5\sqrt{10}-6\sqrt[3]{5} & = \\ 5\sqrt{10}+(2\sqrt[3]{5}-6\sqrt[3]{5}) & = \\ 5\sqrt{10}+(2-6)\sqrt[3]{5} & = \\ 5\sqrt{10}-4\sqrt[3]{5} & \end{aligned}
$$
